clue.text: One can get a rise out of this, but to a degree a ruler gets what one might take in a hurry.

definitions.text: One can get a rise out of this

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
a king is a ruler

parts.words: what one might take in a hurry
parts.note: to 'take a powder' is American slang for leaving in a hurry

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that rises, then a ruler with a degree grabbing what a fleeing person takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' joins the king to the powder; 'take a powder' means to clear off quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Baking powder is the leavening agent that makes dough or batter rise in the oven.

clue.text: A female singer on a get-together in Pennsylvania.

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in Pennsylvania, a noun for the town

indicators.note: the clue's get-together has the pieces join up one after another

parts.note: an alto is a singer with the low female voice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman sings at a gathering somewhere in Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: Altoona is a railway town in central Pennsylvania, so it is a place in that state.

clue.text: Igloo?

parts.note: an igloo is literally a dwelling built of frozen blocks; the question mark flags the playful literal reading

explanation.walkthrough: An icehouse is really a store for keeping ice, but read literally it is a house made of ice, which an igloo is.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped shelter built from blocks of snow, a home made of frozen water.

clue.text: See 11 across
The founder of a Turkish dynasty–one of Morocco's many.

definitions.text: The founder of a Turkish dynasty
definitions.meaning: first sense: ... I, who founded the Ottoman line of sultans
second sense: ..., or Othman, is a common Muslim given name, borne by many Moroccan men

explanation.walkthrough: The Ottomans take their name from Osman, their founder; the same name is common across the Muslim world, Morocco included.
explanation.definitionFit: Osman I founded the Ottoman Empire around 1300, and his name is a widespread Muslim forename.

clue.text: Sounds like Little Richard more than once found a little antelope!

indicators.note: the clue says the answer is heard as the spoken words that follow

parts.note: Little Richard is Dick, the pet form of Richard; said more than once gives DICK DICK

explanation.surface: As if the rock singer Little Richard had stumbled on a small antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' says the answer is heard as the words that follow. 'Little Richard' is not the singer but the short form of the name, Dick, and 'more than once' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The dik-dik is a tiny African antelope, barely knee-high to a person.

clue.text: Part of the area Liz established, as one might find out.

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words supplies the letters, a run straddling the word breaks

parts.note: the letters sit across the word breaks: the end of area, all of Liz, and the start of established

explanation.surface: A woman named Liz set up some district, as one could discover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' says only some of the following letters are used: they run from the end of 'area' through 'Liz' into the start of 'established'.
explanation.definitionFit: To realize something is to come to understand or discover it.

clue.text: When amateur ornithologists do, it's because one is spotted, according to a signal from the camera operator.

definitions.text: When amateur ornithologists do, it's because one is spotted
definitions.meaning: first sense: birdwatchers keep their eyes on a bird once one has been seen

definitions.text: a signal from the camera operator
definitions.meaning: second sense: the photographer's old call telling a sitter to look at the lens

explanation.walkthrough: Old photographers held up a toy bird by the camera to make children look at the lens, hence the call. BIRDY is a variant spelling of birdie.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works literally for birders following a sighted bird and idiomatically as a photographer's cue to look up.

clue.text: Somewhat dated description for one of "two on the aisle."

definitions.text: Somewhat dated description for one of "two on the aisle."

parts.words: Somewhat dated description for one of "two on the aisle."
parts.note: 'two on the aisle' sounds like a pair of theatre seats, but here it is a couple walking up the church aisle at their wedding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Two on the aisle' is the classic request for a pair of theatre tickets, but the aisle meant is the church's, walked by a wedding couple; the old-fashioned phrase describes one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest bride reddening at her wedding is the stock old-fashioned image of a woman marrying.

clue.text: It could be the worker to carry what looks like an aardvark.

parts.note: a worker ant is the standard crossword worker
to bear is to carry

explanation.surface: Some labourer lugging something resembling an aardvark.
explanation.definitionFit: Antbear is another name for the aardvark, the burrowing African mammal that feeds on termites.

clue.text: Red-head?

parts.note: reads as someone with ginger hair, but means the head of the Reds, the Soviet communists

explanation.walkthrough: In 1989 the man leading the Soviet Union, the Reds, was its general secretary and president; the question mark signals the pun on someone with red hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorbachev was leader of the Soviet Communist Party, and communists are called Reds.

clue.text: State the responsibility of Mario!

parts.note: reads as a demand to describe someone's duty, but asks whose charge the State is: Mario, the governor of New York in 1989

explanation.walkthrough: Mario Cuomo was governor of New York State from 1983 to 1994, so the State was his responsibility; the clue asks for his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York governor Mario Cuomo is the Mario whose job was running a state.

clue.text: Do they get paid regularly in auntie's establishment?

indicators.note: the letters are set up afresh, establishing a new order for them

explanation.surface: A question about whether staff at an aunt's shop or house earn steady wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'establishment' looks like the aunt's shop, but it is the signal to set the letters of IN and AUNTIES up in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuity is a fixed sum paid out each year, so annuities are payments made at regular intervals.

clue.text: Sends on the receipts–even if they don't go over the water.

definitions.text: Sends on the receipts–even if they don't go over the water.

parts.words: Sends on the receipts–even if they don't go over the water.
parts.note: the word looks as if it means shipping across the sea, but forwarding goods received from one carrier to another needs no voyage

explanation.walkthrough: The word seems to promise ships crossing water, yet it means moving incoming goods on from one carrier to the next, by land as readily as by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To transship is to transfer cargo from one vessel or vehicle to another for onward carriage.

clue.text: Unnaturally rapid, came to help in an emergency, perhaps.

indicators.note: the letters are put in an unnatural, altered order

explanation.surface: Someone rushed abnormally fast to give aid in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came' looks like part of the definition, but it joins 'rapid' as the letters that 'Unnaturally' tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is a trained medical worker sent out to treat people at accidents and crises, an example of emergency aid.

clue.text: "Turnpike" might describe it, if you take military cover.

indicators.note: the quoted word describes the answer: its first half, turn, is the instruction applied to its second half

parts.note: the quoted word splits as turn plus pike: its first half is the instruction to turn the second half's letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: Something a toll road could describe, if you are hiding as a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A turnpike is a toll road, but 'might describe it' says the word itself spells out the answer: split it, and 'Turn' is the instruction and PIKE the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is the flat-topped peaked cap worn by French soldiers, a piece of army headgear.

clue.text: This location in Pakistan is in bad shape, with the fighting going on!

indicators.note: the fighting goes on after the rearranged letters
shape in bad order, its letters out of their right places

parts.note: fighting is war

explanation.surface: A Pakistani place is in a sorry state because of an ongoing war.
explanation.definitionFit: Peshawar is a city in north-west Pakistan near the Khyber Pass, a well-known location there.

clue.text: The Walrus and the Carpenter had to give a hand to this.

definitions.text: The Walrus and the Carpenter had to give a hand to this.

parts.words: The Walrus and the Carpenter had to give a hand to this.
parts.note: a quotation from Lewis Carroll's poem, where the pair can take only four oysters so as to give a hand to every one

explanation.walkthrough: In Carroll's poem in Through the Looking-Glass the Walrus says 'We cannot do with more than four, to give a hand to each.'
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word of the poem's line is the one meaning every single oyster in turn.

clue.text: Tom on one of the Swiss hills, with a tree here.

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece on another sits above it, so the cat comes first
the a is added along with the rest at the end

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
an alp is a Swiss mountain

explanation.surface: A tomcat on a Swiss slope, with a tree nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The catalpa is a North American and Asian tree with large heart-shaped leaves and long bean pods.

clue.text: What the "spy in the sky" is supposed to be doing? Or one like Simon Legree?

definitions.text: What the "spy in the sky" is supposed to be doing? Or one like Simon Legree?

parts.words: What the "spy in the sky" is supposed to be doing? Or one like Simon Legree?
parts.note: a spy satellite watches from above, and Simon Legree, the slave driver in Uncle Tom's Cabin, supervises workers

explanation.walkthrough: Both readings land on one word: looking down from on high, as a spy satellite does, and supervising labour, the job of Legree in Uncle Tom's Cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is both to watch from above and to supervise workers, so the activity fits satellite and slave driver alike.

clue.text: One wouldn't thank you for showing where to start the fire!

definitions.meaning: second sense, split as two words: inside the fireplace's iron basket

explanation.walkthrough: Read as IN GRATE, the answer is where a fire is laid; read whole, it is an ungrateful person.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is someone who shows no gratitude, and a fire is lit in the grate of a hearth.

clue.text: In Rome, perhaps, or in Spain you might have found such a sheep originally.

definitions.text: in Spain you might have found such a sheep originally.

indicators.note: the letters are a possible version of the words, freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Pondering whether this breed of sheep came from Italy or from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Rome' looks like a place for the sheep, but those two words are the letters to rearrange, as 'perhaps' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The merino, prized for its fine wool, was bred in Spain, which long guarded the breed.

clue.text: Getting along socially? That's where a butterfly might help!

definitions.meaning: first sense: fully involved in what is going on in society

definitions.text: That's where a butterfly might help
definitions.meaning: second sense: the butterfly is a swimming stroke, useful when in the water

explanation.walkthrough: The butterfly here is not the insect but the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the swim is an idiom for being active in fashionable social life, and literally means being in the pool.

clue.text: The merit of a wild throw?

indicators.note: a wild throw sends the letters flying into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking what value a badly aimed throw has.
explanation.definitionFit: Worth is value or merit, the quality of deserving esteem.

clue.text: Ishmael's mother, with a garland to show her off.

indicators.note: the words around her name display it, carrying it inside them

parts.note: the name runs from the last letter of with, through a, into the start of garland

explanation.surface: A biblical mother decked with a wreath to make her look her best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to show her off' means the words display her name inside them: it runs from the end of 'with' through 'a' into 'garland'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Hagar was Sarah's Egyptian handmaid who bore Abraham's son Ishmael.

clue.text: Everything in a wild ride describes one who fools around!

indicators.note: the word everything gives letters set inside the rearranged ones
a wild ride throws its letters about

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A rollicking ride where everybody larks about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ride' looks like part of the picture, but 'wild' rearranges it to DIER, and 'in' puts the word for everything inside that, after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to trifle or flirt idly, so a dallier is a person who messes about.

clue.text: Early lutanist and composer of "The Wise Old Owl and Me."

indicators.note: the title's words compose, that is make up, the name within them

parts.words: The Wise Old Owl and Me.
parts.note: the name runs from the last letter of Old through Owl and

explanation.surface: Crediting an old lute player with writing a quaint song about an owl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composer' looks like part of the definition, since he did write music, but 'composer of' says the title's words make up the name: it runs from the D ending 'Old' through 'Owl and'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dowland was the great English lute player and songwriter of the Elizabethan age.

clue.text: Where we sent mail to GIs, to add to the dental trouble caused by drug handlers.

indicators.note: the post office is joined on in front of the rest

parts.words: Where we sent mail to GIs
parts.note: APO is the US Army Post Office, the address for mail to soldiers abroad
caries is tooth decay

explanation.surface: Wartime letters to soldiers, plus toothache brought on by pharmacists.
explanation.definitionFit: Apothecaries were the old pharmacists who prepared and sold medicines.
